title: Cerrado Mineiro
body:
The Cerrado Mineiro is a high-plain savanna in western Minas Gerais with a long, dry harvest season — ideal conditions for growing sweet, chocolaty, and full-bodied naturally processed coffees. The region is also a pioneer: in 2013, it became Brazil’s first coffee region to earn Denomination of Origin status.
The Cerrado Mineiro Region
The scale here is remarkable. The region spans more than 210,000 hectares across 55 municipalities, where roughly 4,500 producers grow about five million bags of coffee each year. Elevations range from 800 to 1,300 meters. Meanwhile, the well-defined seasons do the real magic: rainy summers ripen the cherries, and the long, dry winters let them dry slowly and evenly. Growers here also invest heavily in technology and quality research, which shows in the cup. Consequently, the Cerrado Mineiro has become Brazil’s benchmark for consistent, naturally processed coffee — and the region behind several of our Cerrado Award-winning microlots .
What’s in the Cup
Expect caramel, chocolate, and nutty flavors, balanced by a mild citric acidity and a full body. The sweetness runs deep, while the finish stays smooth and satisfying. In short, this is classic Brazil in a cup — comforting, generous, and endlessly drinkable. It makes an excellent everyday drip, a rich French press, and a nutty, chocolate-forward espresso that loves milk. Iced or cold brew, it keeps its chocolate depth without turning bitter. title: Child in the Manger by Sinclair B. Ferguson
body: What is Christmas? For many it is a time for holidays, parties, family gatherings, gifts, meals together, music, and special events. For others it can mean unwanted pressure, an increased sense of loneliness, family squabbles, and crowded shops. For those living in the Northern Hemisphere, Christmas takes place at the onset of winter with its cold weather and short days. There are more incidents of depression at Christmas time than at any other time of the year. It is the best of times for some, but the worst of times for others to borrow a phrase from Charles Dickens. The birth of Jesus divided history into two major epochs. Until the dawn of our hyper-sensitive age, even the way we dated events underscored this. From time immemorial every day, every week, every month, every year has been described as either ‘B.C.’ (‘Before Christ’) or ‘A.D.’ (Anno Domini, ‘in the year of our Lord’). Even the modern, pluralistic style abbreviations, B.C.E. (‘Before the Common Era’) and C.E. (‘Common Era’), cannot obliterate the indelible impress of Jesus’ birth. For what makes the ‘Common Era’ so ‘common’? And what explains the dividing line date? The answer is the same: the birth of Jesus. At the very centre of history stands the person of Jesus Christ. And he does so because he is at the centre of God’s story.

Our Seneca Salt Natural Culinary Flake Salt is the only salt you need for cooking, baking or finishing your favorite dish! For a change of pace try our new line of Infused Seneca Salts.
Salt is simple. We all use it and we couldn't survive without this essential element. Most people think of the ocean when they think of salt, but salt deposits occur inland as well and that's the case in the Finger Lakes region of upstate New York where Seneca Salt Company was born far from any seashore.
Seneca Salt begins in salt veins 500 to 2,800 feet below the surface of Seneca Lake. A brine is produced within the salt vein using lake water. title: Emerson Narváez - SL28
body:
MEET THE PRODUCER | Emerson Narváez is a young, second generation coffee producer in the renowned Nariño region of Colombia… but he got a bit of a reluctant start. Emerson explored various professions—serving as a soldier, a builder, and a baker—before fate brought him back to the family business. Once he finally dipped his toes in the proverbial water, Emerson dove all the way in, immersing himself in coffee education, prioritizing crop quality over quantity, and working to improve sustainability practices on his family’s farm.
That farm, Finca el Turpial, is a pretty special place. Located in the village of El Consuelo and situated high on the side of the Andes Mountains, its privileged position grants the farm excellent growing conditions for specialty coffee, including this SL28 lot from Emerson’s September 2024 harvest.
TRUST THE PROCESS | After being handpicked at peak ripeness, whole coffee cherries undergo an initial round of anaerobic fermentation in plastic GrainPro bags, lasting four days. After this, the coffee is de-pulped mechanically and stuffed right back into those GrainPro bags, where it then undergoes an additional 24 hours of anaerobic fermentation—this time in dry mucilage. Finally, the coffee is washed with potable water, the mucilage is removed, and another round of quality sorting takes place via flotation. The remaining cherries are then spread out to sun-dry on raised beds for about 20 days.

The hazelnut coffee that actually tastes like hazelnut — not artificial sweetness, not bitterness. Pure roasted nut perfection.

Smooth without sugar. Rich without cream. The low acid base naturally amplifies the sweetness of the hazelnut flavoring, creating a satisfying, dessert-quality cup that most people drink black. No artificial sweetness. No heavy syrup. Just clean hazelnut richness.
Gentle on your stomach. Extraordinary on your palate. pH 5.7–5.9, verified low acid. The hazelnut coffee you can finally drink every morning without consequences.
LACCSA certified. Available in 2.5 LB Drip Grind or Whole Bean. The hazelnut coffee that redefines the category.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is flavored coffee lower in acid? Not by default. Most flavored coffees retain a pH of 4.8–5.0 regardless of added flavors. Puroast Hazelnut is built on a low acid base (pH 5.7–5.9) — making it the only hazelnut coffee genuinely low in acid while delivering authentic roasted hazelnut flavor.

title: Honduras - Anaerobic Natural - Lopez Family Farm
body:
We are very excited to bring this special coffee to you, directly from Adelmo Lopez's family farm in Honduras. Finca Terrerito is a 5th generation specialty coffee farm located in Copan, Honduras.
This anaerobic coffee is a unique process. The cherries are left intact and placed in sealed tanks for 90+ of fermentation, transforming compounds into acids and alcohols, creating an explosion of unique flavors. The coffee is then dried on raised African beds for an average of 15 days then milled into the final green coffee.
It then arrives to our roasting facility, where we roast the coffee light, preserving the vibrant flavors this process brings. It yields a raspberry forward cup with a winey backend.
The Lopez family farm is certified Organic, Rainforest Alliance, Fair Trade TSA, and Bird Friendly. In addition, they give back to their local community through clean water projects, as well as a school and medical clinic for the surrounded areas.

title: Kona Tropical Punch — 100% Kona Coffee (Light Roast)
body:
Kona Tropical Punch is our most expressive and fruit-forward Kona coffee. Produced from small seasonal lots and roasted light, it showcases how modern fermentation and careful variety selection can unlock a vivid, tropical side of Kona’s volcanic terroir.
This coffee departs intentionally from traditional Kona profiles, offering a brighter, more dynamic cup for those who enjoy acidity-driven, aromatic coffees.
Origin: North Kona, Hawai‘i Roast: Light Varieties: Typica, SL34, Geisha Process: Washed with yeast fermentation Flavor: Lilikoi (passionfruit), orange zest, strawberry papaya, pineapple Body: Silky, wine-like Acidity: Bright, juicy Coffee Review Score: 97 Points
Process & Roast Style
This coffee undergoes a yeast-fermented washed process , where selected yeast strains guide fermentation after pulping, enhancing fruit expression while maintaining the cleanliness of a washed coffee.
Roasted light , the profile is designed to preserve acidity, aromatics, and transparency. Development is intentionally restrained to allow fermentation-derived fruit notes to remain vivid without becoming heavy or winey.
Cup Profile
Expect a lively, aromatic cup with flavors of passionfruit, orange zest, strawberry papaya, and pineapple. Acidity is bright and refreshing, balanced by a silky, wine-like mouthfeel and a long, resonant finish.
Compared to our Kona Classic Medium, this coffee is brighter, fruitier, and more adventurous in style.

Interested in learning more about our roasting process ?
All of our decafs are processed by the Indirect Contact method. The beans are soaked in hot water, which extracts the caffeine and coffee oils. The beans are then removed from the water. A decaffeinating agent is added to the water. The caffeine precipitates out of solution and is removed. The remainder of the decaffeinating agent evaporates out of the water. The coffee beans are reintroduced to the water where they reabsorb their oils. The coffee is then dried and ready for roasting.

This offering is grown in the remote Northern Province of Zambia, near the borders of Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Cultivated at elevations of 1,300-1,600 meters, the region’s rich soils, favorable climate, and abundant freshwater create ideal conditions for high-quality Arabica coffee. With coffee production dating back to 1982, the region remains an important source of employment and economic opportunity for local communities.
Harvested from July through October at peak ripeness, Lupili coffee is primarily fully washed, carefully fermented, and sun-dried on raised beds. The parchment is then rested for approximately six weeks to help stabilize the coffee and preserve its quality before export. Investments in modern milling facilities, irrigation, and agricultural research further support consistent quality and long-term sustainability.
At Lupili Estate, quality goes hand in hand with community development and environmental stewardship. Investments in housing, clean water, energy, and healthcare help improve local livelihoods, while women play an increasingly important role in the workforce and management training. title: Hulikere Estate • India
body:
This is our second year purchasing coffee from Shreedev and Sushmita Hulikere, via our friends at Osito Coffee .
Shreedev and Sushmita manage Hulikere Estate, a sprawling 100 hectare farm, with over 100 year-round employees. This is a big deal: positions like a coffee picker, for example, tend to be a seasonal labor force, and by offering more stable work, Hulikere has a base of a very skilled team that knows what it takes to produce higher quality coffee.
Hulikere Estate is also a part of the KaadKaapi collective, which focuses on integrating the systems of coffee production alongside the natural environment. To put it more clearly: these producers prioritize the health of their farmland and forests before coffee cultivation. They believe that, in the face of our shared climate crisis, conservation of local biodiversity should be the primary goal, using coffee as a tool for that care.
All coffee at Hulikere is hand picked and processed within the same day. Processing techniques include float removal, disc pulping, natural fermentation, and meticulous drying in clay brick yards. This is a massive feat, thanks to their year-round workers, that contributes to the impressive quality of their coffee.
We selected this coffee to continue showcasing Hulikere Estate, as well as highlight the consistency of coffee from Chikmagalur, India. Over the last 3 years, we’ve purchased many coffees from India, and washed lots like this one remind us of what makes India’s terroir so special. Th

Our Rwanada Rushashi Hingakawa is a shade-grown organic and Fair Trade certified, light bodied, soft coffee, with an orange blossom aroma and a clean finish.
This coffee comes from the Abakundakawa cooperative group in the northern province of Gakenke. Abakundakawa means “People Who Love Coffee” in Kinyarwanda and we think the love of coffee is evident in the consistent quality from this group. Abakundakawa, like many other producer groups, gained its well-deserved reputation through the prestigious Cup of Excellence programs.
We are very proud to be offering coffee produced by a group of women within the coop, who have organized themselves as the Hingakawa Women’s Association. The group receives a premium to use for the additional work of lot separation, and to re-invest in programs benefiting the members. The group has already purchased a communal farm and distributed cows, pigs & goats to members, and their next plan is to build a training center to be used for a wide variety of initiatives from child development and nutrition to sewing instruction for additional income. Hingakawa (“Let’s Grow Coffee”) is more of a chant than it is a mere statement; it is a resolution to fight against poverty rather than each other, and with this sentiment they have been able to move forward and heal their community through cooperation and leadership.
